label: rare: y/h/w/m/x input after l/n/g/x context, near original position 3
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps). Activations concentrate on inputs y, h (about 55% of mass), then w, m, x, at the 3rd-5th original position (peak t=3) or the matching copy step where that token is fed back (recall_idx 3-5). They are enriched when earlier tokens include l, n, g, x, i (first_tok l has 7.9x lift). It never fires at t=0-1, on the delimiter, or on mis-copied sequences. Magnitude is fairly flat (median 0.12, max 0.24). The top examples have l/n-heavy prefixes such as l l n m and l n n w. These ingredients are only enrichments: every predicate built from them has precision under 4%, and the best F1 is about 0.06. The feature seems to pick out narrow combinations of prefix tokens that no simple predicate captures.
